claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy-alloy film.
The CuMoTaWV film is produced by DC-magnetron sputtering.
The as-deposited CuMoTaWV film has a nanocrystalline BCC structure.
The unmodified CuMoTaWV film has a room-temperature coefficient of friction near 0.25.
The unmodified CuMoTaWV film reaches a coefficient of friction near 1.5 and experiences increased wear at elevated temperatures.
Approximately 5 vol.% MoS2 nanosheets should be incorporated into the HEA feedstock before film deposition.
Post-deposition annealing at approximately 300 °C enables interfacial bonding and a favorable composite microstructure.
The intervention produces a uniform dispersion of MoS2 nanosheets along grain boundaries and within the CuMoTaWV matrix.
Dispersed MoS2 stabilizes lubricious phases and retards grain growth at high temperatures.
Layered MoS2 provides intrinsic solid lubrication through easy interlayer shear.
Stable MoS2 dispersion in the fine-grained HEA matrix preserves mechanical strength.
Controlled oxidation and preservation of the nanostructure act synergistically at high temperature to maintain low friction and reduced wear.
The MoS2-containing composite maintains high mechanical strength and low friction from room temperature to approximately 600 °C.
The composite coating has an average coefficient of friction below 0.3 throughout the stated temperature range.
The composite coating has a wear rate at least one order of magnitude below that of unmodified CuMoTaWV throughout the stated temperature range.
The improved tribological performance occurs without a marked loss of mechanical strength.
Adding MoS2 beyond approximately 5 vol.% can reduce strength or cause deleterious phase segregation.
The proposed effects may not persist significantly above 600 °C.

contradictions.description: The boundary field describes 5 vol.% MoS2 as an optimal loading, while the uncertainty field says that the optimal MoS2 volume fraction has not been fully established.
